plain_language_definition: The amount you pay every month to keep your plan active.
The amount you pay each calendar year for covered services before the plan starts to share the cost. Copays do not count toward the deductible.
A fixed amount you pay for a covered service, such as a doctor visit.
The percentage of the allowed amount you pay after the deductible has been met.
The most you pay in a calendar year for covered services. Premiums do not count. After you reach it, the plan pays 100 percent of covered in-network services.
A provider that has a contract with Nordlicht Health and accepts the allowed amount as full payment.
A provider without a contract. You pay a higher coinsurance and may be billed the difference.
Approval from Nordlicht Health that is needed before certain services so that they are covered.
A written recommendation from your GP to see a specialist or start a therapy.
A statement that shows what a provider billed, what the plan allowed, what the plan paid and what you owe. It is not a bill.
A request for payment that a provider or member sends to the plan.
A decision that a claim or service is not covered, with the reason.
A request to review a denial.
The list of drugs the plan covers.
A drug with the same active ingredient as a brand-name drug, usually at a lower price.
A drug sold under a manufacturer's trade name.
Check-ups, screenings and vaccinations that aim to prevent illness.
Care for a sudden condition that a reasonable person would believe needs immediate treatment.
Care for a condition that needs attention soon but is not life-threatening.
Care that requires staying in a hospital overnight or longer.
Care that does not require an overnight hospital stay.
A period after enrollment during which a benefit is not yet covered.
A service or situation the plan does not cover.
A health condition that existed before your coverage began.
1 January to 31 December.
The maximum amount the plan recognises for a covered service.
When an out-of-network provider bills you for the difference between its charge and the allowed amount.
The amount a provider charges before any plan adjustment.
A service that the plan pays for under its terms.
The group of providers contracted by the plan.
Your first point of contact for non-emergency care.
A doctor focused on a specific area such as cardiology or dermatology.
A test such as imaging or lab work used to find the cause of symptoms.
A family member covered under your plan.
The yearly period when you can join or change plans.
A period after a missed premium payment during which coverage continues.
The rules used when more than one plan covers the same person.
Care that is needed to diagnose or treat a condition and meets accepted standards.
The number that identifies you to the plan.
A yearly overview of your claims and payments.
